body: The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop shortly before 4 p.m. Eastern time on Friday, November 13, 2026, after a communications outage affected every Air Route Traffic Control Center in the United States. All departures were suspended until further notice, and the FAA later advised crews to expect airborne holding nationwide. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the problem as "a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers" and said FAA technicians were investigating; his initial statement did not identify which system had failed or say when departures would resume. The FAA confirmed the ground stop was implemented "out of an abundance of caution", saying: "There has been a temporary telecommunications outage - out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted. Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis."

The disruption built up through the afternoon. Chicago paused departures first after local controllers encountered communications problems, Houston's George Bush Intercontinental Airport then confirmed it had suspended all departures, and at San Francisco International Airport a spokesperson said aircraft already in the air continued to land while departures were paused. Flightradar24 counted about 3,100 aircraft airborne and bound for US airports during the stop, while FlightAware reported more than 6,500 flights halted. Flightradar24 also reported more than 1,000 flights already canceled by 6 p.m., and Cirium data indicated more than 11,000 flights were still scheduled to depart across the US on Friday, so cancellations were expected to rise sharply.

Law enforcement officials said the ground stop was not the result of a cyberattack, and personnel from the Federal Bureau of Investigation were monitoring the situation, according to CNN. The FAA also said there was no indication the halt was related to the Microsoft outage that affected millions of people worldwide on Thursday. The halt followed the FAA's rollout of a new AI system to manage air traffic, known as the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (SMART), though it was not clear that the telecommunications outage was directly related. The stop was the second nationwide halt since the September 11, 2001 attacks and the first since January 2023, when the FAA's Notice to Air Missions system failed and departures were grounded for about an hour and a half. Hours before the stop, the White House and the Transportation Department had asked Congress for an additional $30.1 billion for aviation infrastructure modernization, including $10.1 billion for air traffic control upgrades.

The FAA lifted the nationwide ground stop at around 8:30 p.m. Eastern time, allowing flights to resume, though airlines warned it could take days to restore normal schedules. Multiple sources later reported that the FAA's telecommunications infrastructure rebooted during an update to a private communications network that connects the nationwide air traffic control system, and the system then crashed, causing the communications outage, according to CBS News; the network is reportedly operated by L3Harris.
en.summary: The FAA halted all departures across the United States on Friday after a communications outage affected every air route traffic control center, the second nationwide ground stop since the September 11 attacks; airborne flights were allowed to keep flying while technicians investigated. The FAA lifted the stop at around 8:30 p.m. Eastern time, allowing flights to resume.
en.title: FAA orders nationwide ground stop as communications outage hits air traffic control centers

body: 美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）於2026年11月13日星期五美東時間下午4時前不久下令全美地面停飛，原因是通訊中斷影響全美每一座航路交通管制中心。所有出發航班暫停至另行通知，FAA其後建議機組人員預期全美各機場將出現空中等待。美國運輸部長尚恩·達菲表示，問題是影響所有航路交通管制中心的通訊問題，FAA技術人員正在調查中；他的初步聲明未指明是哪一個系統故障，也未提供出發航班恢復的時間。FAA表示，此舉出於高度謹慎，空中航班獲准繼續飛行，國際航班將逐案處理，每一架航班均已掌握。

停飛命令下達前已有徵兆：芝加哥航管人員遇到通訊問題後率先暫停出發航班，休士頓喬治布希洲際機場隨後確認暫停所有出發航班；舊金山國際機場發言人表示，已經在途的飛機繼續降落，出發航班則暫停。據Flightradar24統計，地面停飛期間約有3,100架飛機正在空中飛往美國機場；據FlightAware統計，逾6,500架次航班停擺。Flightradar24另指出，截至當晚6時已有逾1,000架次航班取消；據Cirium資料，13日全美仍有逾11,000架次航班預定出發，取消架次預料將大幅增加。

執法官員表示，此次地面停飛並非網路攻擊所致，美國聯邦調查局（FBI）正監控情勢。FAA也表示，沒有跡象顯示此次停飛與13日影響全球數百萬人的微軟服務中斷有關。此次停飛也發生在FAA推出管理空中交通的新人工智慧系統之後，該系統名為空域、航路與航跡戰略管理系統（SMART），但目前尚不清楚電信中斷是否與其直接相關。此次停飛是2001年9月11日恐怖攻擊以來第二次全美地面停飛，也是2023年1月以來首次；2023年1月11日，FAA的飛航任務通知系統故障，全美出發航班停擺約90分鐘。停飛發生數小時前，白宮與美國運輸部才向國會要求額外301億美元用於航空基礎設施現代化，其中包括101億美元用於空中交通管制升級。
FAA隨後於美東時間晚間8時30分左右解除全美地面停飛，航班獲准恢復起飛，但航空公司警告可能需要數日才能恢復正常班表。另據多家媒體報導，FAA的電信基礎設施當日因私人通訊網路更新而重新啟動，系統隨後當機導致通訊中斷；該網路據報由L3Harris營運。
zh.summary: 美國聯邦航空總署13日因通訊中斷影響全美航路管制中心，下令全美航班地面停飛，為2001年9月11日以來第二次全美停飛；空中航班獲准繼續飛行，技術人員正在調查原因。停飛已於美東時間晚間8時30分左右解除，航班獲准恢復起飛。
zh.title: 航管通訊中斷：美國聯邦航空總署下令全美航班地面停飛
